column1: # Board row status: the one declaration of the machine (docs/briefs/DECISION-BRIEF-declared-state-machines.md).
# Every reader derives its state set from this file: backlog.sh (`states`, `machine`), board-writeback.sh,
# lib/sync/sync_core.py (and the sync sources through it), lib/sync/sweep/board-health.
# tests/test-meta-declared-states.sh fails when a script hardcodes the vocabulary again.
# Columns are TAB-separated: state, class, next.
#   class  active    work is open and moving
#          hold      paused on purpose; resumes into any active state
#          terminal  closed by a human decision; a move out of it is a reopen, and `set` says so
#   next   the forward path a caller normally takes from this state, space-separated, `-` for none.
#          Advisory: `set` accepts any declared state from any non-terminal state (hand repairs,
#          reconcile, and sync legitimately jump), so this column answers "where do I go next",
#          never "what is allowed". A move back to an EARLIER active row (file order) also prints
#          a stderr notice and still writes.
# Order matters: it is the render order of `backlog.sh board` and of `states`.
queued
claimed
speccing
validated
executing
